summary: Makes onSave async and writes a JSON snapshot of the in-memory store to data/notes.json after each save.

findings.title: Async onSave returns a Promise to res.end
findings.problem: onSave now returns a Promise, but dispatch in src/router.js:7 returns it unchanged and src/main.js:9 passes it to res.end. res.end rejects a Promise chunk with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, and nobody awaits or catches the Promise.
findings.consequence: Every POST /save/<id> request throws inside the request handler, which crashes the server process. A failed writeFile also becomes an unhandled rejection because no caller observes the Promise.
findings.fix: Make the request handler in src/main.js async and await dispatch before calling res.end, with a try/catch around it. Alternatively keep onSave synchronous and use writeFileSync.

findings.title: Snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: onSave gains a new file-write side effect and becomes async, but the repository has no test files. No test exercises the snapshot write or the new return shape.
findings.consequence: The caller break in src/main.js and future snapshot regressions go unnoticed. Someone finds them only by running the server by hand.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls onSave, awaits it, and asserts the snapshot file contains the saved id. Add a test that calls dispatch through the HTTP handler and checks the response body is a string.
